title: Multi-Head Attention
motto: One attention head learns one relation at a time. Eight heads learn eight. Heads are free. Take more of them.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: One attention head learns one relation at a time. Eight heads learn eight. Heads are free. Take more of them.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A single self-attention head computes one attention matrix. That matrix captures one kind of relationship — usually the one that minimizes loss on whatever the training signal is. If your data has subject-verb agreement, co-reference, long-range discourse, and syntactic chunking all tangled together, a single head smears them into a single soft-max distribution and loses half the signal.

The fix from the 2017 Vaswani paper: run several attention functions in parallel, each with its own Q, K, V projections, and concatenate the outputs. Each head operates in a smaller subspace of dimension `d_model / n_heads`. Total parameters stay the same. Expressive power goes up.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Multiple heads attend to different relationship types. Concatenate heads then project.
